clue.text: Go ahead carrying my French energy drink

indicators.note: a word that carries something holds it inside itself, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: to lead is to go ahead of others
French for 'my' (masculine)
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone offers a French drink that gives them a burst of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my French' means the French word for my, not something French belonging to the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is a sweet soft drink flavoured with citrus juice.

clue.text: First off, get rid of irritation

indicators.note: the opening letter is taken off, leaving the rest of the word

blocks.note: to ditch something is to get rid of it

explanation.surface: Advice to deal with an annoyance by dropping it straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a skin irritation that makes you want to scratch, and also a figurative annoyance.

clue.text: A line crossing Italian street's home to birds

indicators.note: the outer letters straddle the street, so the street ends up in the middle of them

blocks.note: taken as written
via is Italian for street or road
RY is the crossword abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A railway line runs across a street in Italy where birds have made their home.
explanation.walkthrough: A and RY wrap around VIA. The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviary is a large enclosure where captive birds are kept and live.

clue.text: Compliment is less spirited

blocks.note: first meaning: to praise someone, often insincerely
second meaning: comparative of an adjective describing a drink gone dull

explanation.surface: Praise from someone who seems rather downcast about giving it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half as 'is flatter': more lacking in fizz or liveliness, the comparative of flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatter is to pay compliments; flatter is also the comparative of flat, meaning dull or listless.

clue.text: Large insect's under tip of pampas grass in tub

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its very first letter
in a down entry, being under something means coming after it in the grid

blocks.note: the opening letter of pampas
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
an ant is an insect; the 's is 'is'
grass and pot are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A big insect is crawling beneath the top of some pampas grass planted in a tub.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'under' puts L and ANT after P. Grass is not the plant here but slang for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant pot is a container, much like a tub, in which a plant is grown.

clue.text: Intended to reflect

blocks.note: first meaning: an adjective for something done on purpose
second meaning: a verb, to think something over carefully

explanation.walkthrough: The word changes pronunciation between its two senses: the adjective ends '-rut', the verb ends '-rate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberate act is one done on purpose; to deliberate is to consider or ponder at length.

clue.text: Lots of dogs quietly disappearing

indicators.note: the letter meaning 'quietly' vanishes from the word for the dogs

blocks.note: poodles are a breed of dog
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A pack of dogs slipping silently away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots of dogs' reads as one phrase, but 'Lots' alone is the definition and 'of' the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is an informal word for a great quantity or abundance of something.

clue.text: Revels in ruin of VAT files

definitions.note: plural noun for a singular answer; a festival is a time of revels

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone takes glee in the destruction of their tax paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax; 'Revels in' looks like 'enjoys', but 'in' is only the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A festival is an organised period of celebration and merrymaking, in other words revels.

clue.text: Stretch out, then squat to keep out of sight

blocks.note: to lie is to stretch out flat
something squat is short and close to the ground

explanation.surface: Instructions for hiding: lie flat, then crouch down so no one spots you.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low is an idiom meaning to stay hidden and avoid attention.

clue.text: Companion's carrying very large truncheon

indicators.note: the companion carries the other piece inside, holding it within its letters

blocks.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
OS is outsize, the clothing-size label

explanation.surface: Someone's friend is carrying a huge club.
explanation.walkthrough: CH holds OS. A Companion of Honour is a member of a British honours order.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosh is a short heavy club or bludgeon, the British term for a weapon like a truncheon.

clue.text: Not as troubled against weakened top grade football team

indicators.note: troubled words are disturbed and stirred up, so their letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
v is short for versus, against
someone ill is weakened by sickness
A is the highest exam grade

explanation.surface: A footballer, less upset than expected, faces a depleted top-division side.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is a Premier League football club from Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston Villa is a professional English football club based in Birmingham, so it is a football team.

clue.text: Crop both sides and finally ease into alcove

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the following word
the earlier pieces go inside the word for the alcove

blocks.note: the two sides are right and left, R and L
the last letter of ease
a bay is a recess or alcove in a wall or room

explanation.surface: Instructions for trimming something at both edges and gently fitting it into a recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop' looks like an instruction to cut, but it is the noun: a cereal grown in fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Barley is a cereal grain grown on farms, an example of an agricultural crop.

clue.text: Penultimate bus at Barking left before time I arrived

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the words beside it are scrambled
before tells us the scrambled group comes ahead of the next pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
T is the abbreviation for time
I is the Roman numeral for one; 'arrived' only rounds off the scene

explanation.surface: Someone catches the second-to-last bus at Barking, a district of east London, after a long wait.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a real London place name, but here it means crazy. 'Arrived' adds nothing to the letters, a slightly loose finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Last but one is a plain idiom for the item immediately preceding the final one, which is what penultimate means.

clue.text: English reporters tucked into very strong coffee

indicators.note: something tucked into another thing sits snugly inside it

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
the press is the collective name for reporters
so means very, as in 'so good'

explanation.surface: Journalists from England knocking back extremely potent coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very strong coffee' reads as one phrase, but 'very' is wordplay and only 'strong coffee' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An espresso is a concentrated coffee brewed by forcing hot water through finely ground beans.

clue.text: URL for Guardian Live's put in

definitions.note: a URL is the address that names a website, so it stands for one here

indicators.note: in tells us one word goes inside the word before it

blocks.note: the editorial 'we' a newspaper such as the Guardian uses of itself
to be is to live or exist
to sit something somewhere is to put or set it there

explanation.surface: A note on what web address to enter for the Guardian's live coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Newspapers speak of themselves as 'we' in leaders. The 's is 'has': Live has put in. URL as definition is loose, the address standing for the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A URL is the address typed into a browser to reach a website, so it loosely stands for the online site itself.

clue.text: Reportedly intended to fill hills with badgers

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word is taken by its sound
a piece that fills another goes inside it

blocks.note: meant means intended
tors are rocky hills, as on Dartmoor in south-west England

explanation.surface: A story of hills meant to be filled with badgers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badgers' looks like the animals but is the verb: to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger is to pester persistently, and torments as a verb means the same harassment.

clue.text: Get very excited when second XI's promoted

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a football or cricket team has eleven players
a promoted team has gone up a division

explanation.surface: Fans of the reserve team get carried away when it wins promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second XI' reads as a reserve side, but second is S and XI is a team.
explanation.definitionFit: To get steamed up is to become agitated or worked up about something, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Elated having finished in front of cycling field, including Tour leader

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
cycling suggests going round and round, so these letters are turned about
the jumbled word includes, or holds, the leading letter inside it
in front of places one piece ahead of the other in the answer

blocks.note: when time is up it has finished
taken as written
the first letter of Tour

explanation.surface: A rider is thrilled at crossing the line ahead of the cycling field, which included the Tour de France leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Uplifted means raised in spirits, cheered and happy, which is what elated means.

clue.text: Calm about vote breaking new deal

indicators.note: a new version of the word is made by rearranging its letters
the vote breaks into the other word, splitting it apart

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written
a cross on a ballot paper marks a vote

explanation.surface: A cool-headed view of a ballot that has disrupted a fresh agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxed means free from tension or anxiety, so a relaxed person is calm.

clue.text: Scouts do stick first of badges on right sleeve in the middle

indicators.note: first of points to the opening letter of each of the next two words
only the central letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: to jam is to stick fast
opening letters of badges and on
R is the abbreviation for right
the two central letters of sleeve

explanation.surface: Instructions for sewing a Scout's badges onto the middle of a right sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scouts do' looks like the subject of a sentence, but 'do' is the noun: a party or gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large rally or gathering of Scouts, a do in the sense of a social event.

clue.text: Heading off, Dave picked up new road

indicators.note: the name loses its head, its opening letter
picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: taken as written before losing its head
spelt to sound like the word new

explanation.surface: Dave sets off and hears about a new road.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad street, often tree-lined, so it is a kind of road.

clue.text: Majority gutted about Klee work lacking oomph

indicators.note: a gutted word has its insides removed, leaving only its outer letters
work suggests the name is worked over and reshaped
the outer letters go round, or about, the other piece

blocks.note: first and last letters of majority
taken as written; Paul Klee was a Swiss-German painter

explanation.surface: Most critics are disappointed that a painting by Klee seems feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Klee work' reads as a painting by the artist, but 'work' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To act meekly is to behave timidly and submissively, without force, energy or assertiveness.

clue.text: Mum's fine coming back without Edward to manage

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the word reads in the opposite direction
without here means outside, so it goes around the next piece

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mum
OK means fine
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Mum is managing fine back home without Edward around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense, outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To make do is to manage with whatever limited resources are available, a common idiom.

clue.text: Take bag containing article and lose job

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: to take something is to get it
a sack is a large bag
the definite article

explanation.surface: An employee walks off with a bag holding an item and is fired.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the sack is an informal idiom meaning being dismissed from employment, so you lose your job.

clue.text: Handy having editor back on newspaper

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for editor in the opposite direction

blocks.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A useful editor has come back to work at the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places one piece before the other. The FT is the Financial Times, a London business daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft and handy both describe someone skilful and neat with their hands.

clue.text: Some reversal in Tyne dockland's decline

indicators.note: some of the words means part of them, a run of letters inside
the letters sit in the words written in the opposite direction

blocks.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A news item about the downturn in the docks along the River Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decline' looks like the noun, a fall, but is the verb: to refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny someone something is to refuse it, the same as declining a request.

clue.text: Turn up with new mesh box for strawberries

indicators.note: turning the short word around makes it read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
net is a mesh of crossed threads

explanation.surface: Someone arrives with a fresh net container of strawberries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' looks like 'arrive', but Turn signals reversal and up is its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A punnet is a small square basket or carton in which soft fruit like strawberries is sold.

clue.text: Object to incense as risk

blocks.note: an end is an object or aim
to anger someone is to incense them

explanation.surface: Someone protests at burning incense because of the fire hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like the verb, to protest, but is the noun: a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger is to put at risk, and risk as a verb means expose to danger.
